title: Third floor guest rooms
goal: A practitioner can read this escape plan at a glance: Third floor guest rooms.

rubric.must: A visible YOU ARE HERE marker, legend, and two marked exits are present.
Primary and secondary routes visibly lead from the marker to separate exits.
A reader can visually follow the principal flow or relationship from beginning to end.
Key labels remain legible and attached to the correct visible elements.
Lines and symbols do not visually imply unintended connections.

ideal.notes: Drafted by Codex from the source, the rubric and the evacuation/iso exemplar, without seeing the engine's own output.

review.evidence: The drawing clearly presents the third-floor guest-room layout, a prominent YOU ARE HERE marker in Room 302, two distinct green escape routes leading west to Stair A and east to Stair B, and two visibly marked final exits. Key room, corridor, stair, extinguisher, assembly-point, and legend labels are legible and correctly associated.

items.evidence: A visible YOU ARE HERE marker appears in Room 302; the full legend is visible at right; EXIT markings appear at both Stair A and Stair B.
The solid primary route leads left from the marker through the corridor to Stair A and its west exit, while the segmented alternative route leads right to Stair B and its east exit.
Directional arrowheads make both paths readable from the Room 302 marker through the corridor to their respective stairs and exits.
YOU ARE HERE, room numbers 301–307, Corridor, Lift Lobby, Stair A, Stair B, EXIT, ABC, and ASSEMBLY POINT are visibly legible and placed beside the corresponding elements.
The two route styles are differentiated in the legend and visibly terminate at separate exits without implying unintended room or stair connections.
